title: The Madwoman in the Attic

vibeProfile.oneLine: Re-reading the great Victorian women writers, and the rage they had to hide.

summary: Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar's landmark of feminist literary criticism re-reads the great nineteenth-century women writers, from Austen and the Brontes to Dickinson, arguing that they wrote within, and against, a male tradition that offered them only the roles of angel or monster. The 'madwoman' of the title, Bertha in Jane Eyre, becomes a figure for the rage such writers had to hide or disguise. Sweeping and dense, it reshaped how the Victorian canon is taught and read.
whyReadIt: The book that changed how we read nineteenth-century women writers. Dense but transformative, with Jane Eyre's madwoman at its heart.

funFacts.text: Its title comes from Bertha Mason, the 'madwoman' locked in the attic of Jane Eyre.
